question: Let \(f(n)=\dfrac{x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n}{n},\) where \(n\) is a positive integer. If \(x_k=(-1)^k,\) \(k=1,\) \(2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(n,\) the set of possible values of \(f(n)\) is:
solution:
The terms are \(-1,1,-1,1,\ldots\), so every adjacent pair has sum \(0\). If \(n\) is even, all terms pair off. If \(n\) is odd, one final \(-1\) remains. Therefore
\[
f(n)=\begin{cases}
0,&n\text{ even},\\
-\dfrac1n,&n\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Every positive integer is either even or odd, so these cases give all possible values. The value \(0\) occurs, for example, at \(n=2\); each negative value occurs at its corresponding positive odd index. Hence the exact range is
\[
\boxed{\{0,-1,-\tfrac13,-\tfrac15,\ldots\}}.
\]
Choice C is the intended answer only when its \(-1/n\) is restricted to odd \(n\). As printed, it does not state that restriction. In particular, \(-1/2\) cannot occur: a negative output requires odd \(n\), whereas \(-1/n=-1/2\) would require \(n=2\).
